# @aszura/marram-browser

> The browser half of Marram's connect and sign-in flows. Your backend mints a short-lived token;
> the package makes a PKCE pair on click, runs `init` directly against Marram with that token,
> keeps the verifier (with the provider, flow id and your state) in that tab's `sessionStorage`,
> navigates to the provider, and on return finishes the flow. It never sees the API key. Includes
> optional React bindings at `@aszura/marram-browser/react`. No dependencies.

This file is for AI coding assistants. Follow the rules first; the reference follows.

## Rules

1. **Every flow starts with a token.** `connect(provider, { token })` and
   `signIn(provider, { token })` are the only ways to start. Your backend mints the token with
   `marram.connectToken({ externalUserId })` / `signInToken()`; minting is local signing, not an
   API call. Never put a Marram **API key** or signing secret in browser code.
2. **Pass `token` as a function that fetches one.** It runs on click, so the ten minutes start with
   the flow. It may resolve a string or `{ token, baseUrl? }`. A token starts exactly one flow; a
   second `connect` with it answers `CONNECT_TOKEN_REUSED`. A refused `connect` doesn't spend it,
   so a corrected retry can reuse it. It only has to be valid at the start:
   `finish` can claim with it after it expires, so never mint a long-lived token for a slow sign-in.
3. **Who claims.** A `connect` is claimed by `finish()` directly against Marram by default, and
   `result.data` is `{ status: 'connected', jti }`, never connection fields. With
   `claim: 'server'`, or for any **sign-in**, `finish({ url })` posts to your endpoint, which claims
   with the API key. Use `claim: 'server'` when your server must see the claim. It doesn't give a
   slow provider sign-in more time: the user has ten minutes with the provider either way, and the
   thirty-minute wait for `claim` starts after that step.
4. **Finish endpoint contract:** receives JSON `{ provider, flowId, codeVerifier, claimCode, ...body }`
   (or `sessionKey`), calls `claim(provider, key, codeVerifier, claimCode)`, stores the result
   against the logged-in user, and answers any JSON. That answer becomes `result.data`. The
   `claimCode` is the one-time code on the redirect URL: `finish()` reads it there and sends it
   on, and Marram refuses a claim without it.
5. **Redirects.** A `redirectUrl` in the token wins and the option here is ignored. Without one, the
   `redirectUrl` option (default: the current page without query/hash) must be on the environment's
   redirect allowlist, and a set allowlist binds the token's URL too; anything else answers
   `REDIRECT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED`. Never sign a URL from the request unchecked.
6. **Carry app context with `state`, not the URL or your session.** `state` is kept in the tab and
   comes back as `result.state` from `finish`. JSON only; it is never sent anywhere.
7. **Same tab start to finish.** `sessionStorage` is per tab. The provider must redirect back to
   the tab that started the flow (normal redirects do). Don't open the authorization URL in a new
   tab or popup.
8. **`finish` claims once.** Marram allows one claim per flow, so a reload can't replay it. It
   keeps the pending flow and the URL until the claim settles, so when `error.retryable` is true,
   call `finish` again or reload. It's safe to call on every load of the redirect page; it returns
   `null` on an ordinary visit.
9. **With a client-side router, pass `cleanUrl`.** The default `history.replaceState` is invisible
   to React Router and Next.js. `cleanUrl: (path) => navigate(path, { replace: true })` (React
   Router) or `cleanUrl: (path) => router.replace(path)` (Next.js) keeps the router in sync.
10. **Next.js App Router: client components only.** `useMarramFinish`, `useMarramStart` and
    `MarramButton` need `'use client'` at the top of the file that uses them.
11. **If the app already has an HTTP client** (axios instance, bearer tokens, refresh, `{ data }`
    envelopes), use it inside the `token` function, and pass `send` to `finish` instead of `url`.
    `send(payload)` delivers the payload however the backend wants it and resolves what becomes
    `result.data`. `send` excludes `url`, `headers`, `credentials` and `fetch`. The script tag's
    `data-finish` only supports `url`.
12. **Running `init` and `claim` yourself?** Don't use this package. Make the PKCE pair on the
    server, keep the verifier in the user's session, and follow the server SDK's flow.
13. **Draw the buttons from `listProviders({ token })`.** It takes the same connect token (listing
    doesn't spend it) and returns the providers this user can connect, each with `integrations`,
    and per integration `authTypes`, `connected` and `connectionStatus`. Pass the entry's
    `integrationKey` and one of its `authTypes` to `connect`; the list doesn't say which integration
    is the default. Show "Reconnect" for `connectionStatus: 'reauth_required'`. Never write a
    backend route for this, and never cache the list: it is per user.
14. **After a flow, `finish()` is the truth.** Mark the provider connected from its result, then
    `reload()` the list if you show it; a list fetched right away can lag by up to ~30 s.
15. **Offer "Disconnect" with `disconnect(provider, { token, integrationKey? })`.** It takes a connect
    token, disconnects the token's own user, and needs no backend route. The token needn't name a
    provider. Each token disconnects once and can't start a flow afterwards, so pass a function that
    mints a fresh one. Update the page from its result, not a reloaded list. Disconnecting leaves
    the user's webhooks running until your server deletes them.
16. **Draw a login page from `listIdentityProviders({ token })`.** Use a sign-in token: listing
    doesn't spend it, and `signIn` refuses a connect token. It returns the providers enabled for
    sign-in, each with `integrations` of `integrationKey` and `label`. Pass the entry's
    `integrationKey` to `signIn`. Never write a backend route for this.
17. **Start a manual webhook setup with `setUpWebhook(provider, { token, integrationKey?, redirectUrl? })`.**
    It takes a connect token for an already-connected user, sends them to Marram's hosted setup
    form (`setupUrl`) and they land back on `redirectUrl`; there's no `finish`. It spends the token.
    Marram picks the `webhookKey`: a custom key or metadata needs the server SDK's `initManual`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @aszura/marram-browser
```

No-build alternative: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@aszura/marram-browser/dist/marram.min.js"></script>`
sets `window.Marram`, and runs `finish` if the tag has `data-finish="/your/finish/endpoint"`.

## Vanilla usage

```ts
import { connect, signIn, finish, listProviders, MarramError } from '@aszura/marram-browser';

const getToken = () => fetch('/marram/token', { method: 'POST' }).then((r) => r.json());

// Page load: the providers this user can connect, with their connection state.
const providers = await listProviders({ token: getToken }); // throws LIST_FAILED
const [provider] = providers;
const [integration] = provider.integrations; // { integrationKey, label, authTypes, connected, connectionStatus }

// Connect button:
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  connect(provider.providerKey, {
    token: getToken, // fresh token on click
    integrationKey: integration.integrationKey,
    auth: integration.authTypes[0],
    state: { returnTo: '/settings?tab=mail' },
  }).catch(showError);
});

// Page at your redirectUrl:
try {
  const result = await finish<{ status: string }, { returnTo: string }>();
  if (result === null) {
    // not a Marram redirect
  } else if (result.ok) {
    // result.kind: 'connection' | 'session', result.provider, result.key,
    // result.data ({ status: 'connected', jti }), result.state
    location.replace(result.state.returnTo);
  } else {
    // user declined / provider error: result.error, result.errorMessage,
    // result.state (from the flow this tab started last, or undefined)
  }
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof MarramError && error.code === 'VERIFIER_NOT_FOUND') {
    // started in another tab/browser, or already used. Start again.
  }
}
```

Your server claims a connect:

```ts
connect('google', { token: getToken, claim: 'server' });
// …then on return:
const result = await finish({ url: '/marram/finish' }); // result.data is your endpoint's JSON
```

Sign-in: the token starts it, your backend always claims it.

```ts
signIn('google', { token: getSignInToken }); // minted with redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/signed-in'
// …then on return:
await finish({ url: '/marram/finish' });
```

Through an existing HTTP client:

```ts
// Backend answers { data: { token, baseUrl } }
connect('google', { token: () => api.post('/marram/token').then((r) => r.data.data), claim: 'server' });

// Claim through the same client; p already has provider, key, codeVerifier and claimCode
finish({ send: (p) => api.post('auth', p).then((r) => r.data) });
```

The script build's `data-finish` fires `marram:finished` (detail: `FinishResult`) or
`marram:error` on `document`.

## React

```tsx
'use client'; // Next.js App Router
import { MarramButton, useMarramStart, useMarramFinish } from '@aszura/marram-browser/react';

<MarramButton token={getToken} provider="google" state={{ returnTo: '/settings' }} onError={(e) => toast(String(e))}>
  Connect Google
</MarramButton>;

function Connected() {
  const navigate = useNavigate(); // React Router; Next.js: const router = useRouter() from 'next/navigation'
  const { loading, result, error } = useMarramFinish<{ status: string }, { returnTo: string }>({
    cleanUrl: (path) => navigate(path, { replace: true }), // Next.js: router.replace(path)
  });
  if (loading) return <p>Finishing…</p>;
  if (error) return <p>Something went wrong. Try connecting again.</p>;
  if (result?.ok === false) return <p>{result.errorMessage ?? 'Cancelled.'}</p>;
  if (result?.ok) return <Navigate to={result.state.returnTo} />;
  return null;
}
```

- `MarramButton`: `<button>` that starts a flow on click with its `token`, `provider`,
  `integrationKey`, `state` and `body` props. It is disabled and `aria-busy` while pending. Other
  props pass through to the button, and `type` defaults to `button`. An `onClick` that calls
  `preventDefault()` cancels the start.
- `useMarramStart(options)` returns `{ start(provider, extras?), pending, error }`, where `extras`
  is `{ state?, body?, redirectUrl?, auth?, integrationKey?, theme? }`. One hook serves a whole menu
  of providers. `start` never throws: failures go to `error` and `onError`, and it resolves
  `undefined`.
- `useMarramIdentityProviders({ token, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch?, enabled? })` is the same
  hook for `listIdentityProviders`, with the same return shape. Start with `flow: 'signIn'`.
- `useMarramProviders({ token, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch?, enabled? })` runs `listProviders`
  once on mount (StrictMode-safe) and returns `{ loading, providers, error, reload }`. `providers`
  is `[]` until loaded and kept across a failed reload; `error` is a `LIST_FAILED`. Call `reload()`
  after a flow finishes. Draw buttons from it:
  `start(p.providerKey, { integrationKey: i.integrationKey, auth: i.authTypes[0] })`.
- Both take `token`, `flow` (`'connect'` default, or `'signIn'`), `claim`, and `connect`'s options.
  A `token` function receives `(provider, extras)`, so a backend can sign the redirect.
- `useMarramFinish(options)` runs `finish` once on mount (StrictMode-safe) and returns
  `{ loading, result, error }`. Pass `enabled: false` to defer, e.g. until your auth has loaded.
  Takes `url` or `send`, plus `body` and `cleanUrl`. An inline `send` that changes every render is
  fine.
- React ≥ 16.8 is an optional peer dependency. Only the `/react` entry point imports it.

## API reference

```ts
type MintedToken = string | { token: string; baseUrl?: string };

type TokenFlowOptions = {
  token: string | (() => MintedToken | Promise<MintedToken>);
  environment?: 'production' | 'staging';   // default 'production'
  baseUrl?: string;                     // overrides environment; include /v1
  redirectUrl?: string;                 // ignored when the token carries one
  auth?: string;                        // default 'oAuth2'; one of the integration's authTypes
  integrationKey?: string;              // sent as x-marram-integration-key; from listProviders
  theme?: 'light' | 'dark';
  body?: Record<string, unknown>;       // extra init fields; the challenge and redirect win on conflict
  state?: unknown;                      // JSON; comes back as finish's result.state
  navigate?: ((url: string) => void) | false; // default location.assign; false = don't navigate
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
};

connect(provider, TokenFlowOptions & { claim?: 'marram' | 'server' }): Promise<StartResult>
signIn(provider, TokenFlowOptions): Promise<StartResult>
// StartResult: { kind: 'connection' | 'session'; provider: string; key: string; authorizationUrl: string }
// key is the flowId (connections) or sessionKey (sign-in)

listProviders({ token, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch? }): Promise<ConnectableProvider[]>
// ConnectableProvider: { providerKey; name; brandColors; brandImages; integrations: ConnectableIntegration[] }
// ConnectableIntegration: { integrationKey; label; authTypes: string[]; connected: boolean;
//   connectionStatus: 'active' | 'pending' | 'reauth_required' | 'error' | 'revoked' | 'inactive' | null }
// GET /environment/providers with the connect token; a token locked to a provider or integration
// lists only that. Never cached (per user).

disconnect(provider, { token, integrationKey?, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch? }): Promise<void>
// DELETE /connections/{provider}/revoke with a connect token; spends the token. Throws DISCONNECT_FAILED.

setUpWebhook(provider, { token, integrationKey?, redirectUrl?, navigate?, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch? }): Promise<WebhookSetup>
// WebhookSetup: { webhookKey; setupUrl; ingressUrl }
// POST /webhooks/{provider}/init with a connect token and body { redirectUrl }; spends the token.
// Navigates to setupUrl unless navigate: false. The user must already be connected
// (CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND / CONNECTION_REVOKED). Throws START_FAILED.

listIdentityProviders({ token, environment?, baseUrl?, fetch? }): Promise<IdentityProvider[]>
// IdentityProvider: { providerKey; name; brandColors; brandImages; integrations: IdentityIntegration[] }
// IdentityIntegration: { integrationKey; label }
// GET /environment/identity-providers with a sign-in token; a locked token lists only that.

// Endpoint options for finish: exactly one of these two shapes.
type FetchEndpointOptions = {
  url: string;                          // your endpoint, POSTed as JSON
  headers?: HeadersInit;                // e.g. CSRF token
  credentials?: RequestCredentials;     // default 'same-origin'
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
};
type SendEndpointOptions = {
  send: (payload: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>; // resolve what becomes result.data
};

finish<T, S>(options?: Partial<FetchEndpointOptions | SendEndpointOptions> & {
  body?: Record<string, unknown>;       // extra payload fields; provider, key, codeVerifier and claimCode win on conflict
  location?: string | URL;              // default location.href
  cleanUrl?: boolean | ((path: string) => void); // default true unless `location` given; a function gets
                                        // the clean path+search+hash to replace through your router
}): Promise<
  | { ok: true; kind: 'connection' | 'session'; provider: string; key: string; data: T; state: S }
  | { ok: false; error: string; errorMessage: string | null; state: S | undefined }
  | null                                // not a Marram redirect
>
// url/send may be omitted only when every flow is a connect that Marram claims.

createPkce(): Promise<{ codeVerifier; codeChallenge; codeChallengeMethod: 'S256' }>
parseRedirect(url): { ok: true; kind: 'connection'; key: null; claimCode: string | null }
  | { ok: true; kind: 'session'; key; claimCode: string | null }
  | { ok: false; error; errorMessage } | null   // connect redirects carry ?status=connected, no key
redirectPath(url): string               // path + search + hash without Marram's params
```

`connect` and `signIn` only navigate to `http(s)` URLs, and reject anything else with
`INVALID_START_RESPONSE`. Pending flows older than one hour are cleaned up the next time a flow
starts; a declined redirect drops the flow this tab started last. A connect redirect carries no key,
so `finish` resolves it to the flow this tab started last.

## Errors

`connect`, `signIn`, `disconnect`, `setUpWebhook`, `listProviders`, `listIdentityProviders` and `finish` throw `MarramError` with `code`, `status` (HTTP
status or null) and `body` (the response, parsed if JSON). Branch on `code`:

| code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `START_FAILED` | Marram's init (`connect`, `signIn` or `setUpWebhook`) answered non-2xx or was unreachable, or the `token` function failed. `apiCode` is Marram's code. |
| `DISCONNECT_FAILED` | The same for `disconnect`. `status: 409` means the token was already used. |
| `LIST_FAILED` | The same for `listProviders` or `listIdentityProviders`, or the answer had no list. A failed page load, not a failed click. |
| `INVALID_START_RESPONSE` | Marram's answer lacked an http(s) `authorizationUrl` or a `flowId`/`sessionKey` (for `setUpWebhook`: an http(s) `setupUrl`, `webhookKey` or `ingressUrl`). |
| `FINISH_FAILED` | Your finish endpoint or Marram's claim answered non-2xx or was unreachable, or `send` rejected. If `retryable` is true (no answer, a 429 or a 5XX), call `finish` again; otherwise start the flow again. |
| `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` | `sessionStorage` blocked (some private modes, sandboxed iframes). |
| `VERIFIER_NOT_FOUND` | This tab didn't start this flow, or it was already used. |

When a `token` function or `send` rejects, the original error is `cause`. `status`/`body` are taken
from `err.status`/`err.body`, else axios-style `err.response.status`/`err.response.data`, else
`null`. A `MarramError` they throw is rethrown unchanged.

Marram's own code is on `error.apiCode`, and `error.message` includes its explanation:
`CONNECT_TOKEN_EXPIRED` (401), `CONNECT_TOKEN_REUSED`
(409), `INVALID_CONNECT_TOKEN` (401/403), `REDIRECT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED` (403), `RATE_LIMITED` (429).
Token calls share one per-IP limit, and a page load now spends one on the list, so a flow costs
three requests: roughly twenty flows a minute per IP.

A provider-side failure or a user who declined is not thrown: `finish` returns
`{ ok: false, error, errorMessage, state }`.

## Server side

Node, with `@aszura/marram-node`:

```ts
const marram = new Marram({ apiKey, signingSecret });

app.post('/marram/token', requireLogin, async (req, res) => {
  const { token } = await marram.connectToken({
    externalUserId: String(req.user.id),
    redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected',
    expiresIn: 600,
  });
  res.json({ token });
});

// Only with claim: 'server', or for sign-in (signInFlow): the finish endpoint.
const flow = connectFlow(marram, { providers: ['google'], redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected' });
app.post('/marram/finish', requireLogin, flow.express.finish(async ({ connection }, req) => {
  await db.markConnected(req.user.id, connection.providerKey);
  return { connected: true };
}));
```

PHP, with `marram/php`:

```php
$token = $marram->connectToken((string) $user->id, expiresIn: 600, redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected')->token;

// Only with claim: 'server', or for sign-in (Marram\SignInFlow): the finish endpoint.
$flow = new Marram\ConnectFlow($marram, ['google'], 'https://yourapp.com/connected');
$flow->serveFinish(fn (array $claimed) => saveAndAnswer($claimed));
```
